name: Shimei
overview: Shimei was a male Levite, distinguished as the son of Jeduthun. He was uniquely identified as the tenth chosen by lot among the singers, set apart to prophesy through musical instruments such as lyres, harps, and cymbals. His role highlights the Levites' special function in worship and prophecy within Israel's religious life.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Shimei' is presented simply as a proper name without a given meaning or divine origin noted in Scripture. Therefore, it is recognized as a straightforward personal name recorded in 1 Chronicles 25:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Shimei was the son of Jeduthun, establishing his lineage within a notable Levitical family. Beyond this filial relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shimei holds significance as one of the select Levite musicians chosen by lot to serve in the temple, emphasizing the God-ordained order and spiritual function of worship through music and prophecy. His appointment as the tenth singer underscores the organized and divinely guided nature of temple service. Through his role, Shimei contributed to the prophetic and worship life of Israel, reflecting the importance of music in biblical prophecy and praise.
